in-0Uhr.title: Buildings: white-domed temples with Khanda symbol
in-0Uhr.summary: Gurdwaras, Sikh temples, have white domes and ornate walls, and often the Khanda symbol. Most common in the north-west (Punjab).

in-0XWk.title: Vehicles: orange and bright green buses
in-0XWk.summary: Orange and bright green buses are typical of the capital region.

in-0bOF.title: Language: Kannada-like script with checkmark marks on top
in-0bOF.summary: In the south-east (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh), the script is very similar to Kannada but often has checkmark-like marks on top of letters.

in-2HRA.title: Plants: spiny cactus-like fences
in-2HRA.summary: This spurge (Euphorbia neriifolia) is common in fences across the west (Gujarat, western Maharashtra, southern Rajasthan).

in-2aSl.title: Plants: coconut trees painted red and white
in-2aSl.summary: Lakshadweep, off the coast of Kerala, has abundant coconut trees, often painted red and white like the Polish flag.

in-3DgL.title: Language: curvy script with wide arches, skull-like
in-3DgL.summary: In the east (Odisha), the script is curvy with wide semi-circles on top of many letters and a wide curve mark above others. Letters look like a skull emoji.

in-3sOG.title: Houses: large hip roofs of corrugated metal
in-3sOG.summary: Large hip roofs of corrugated sheet metal are found in the east (West Bengal) and nearby parts of Bihar and Odisha.

in-58wO.title: Pole: metal poles with holes
in-58wO.summary: Metal poles with holes are common in the south-west (Kerala).

in-5UcB.title: Crops: sugarcane in the north and south-west
in-5UcB.summary: Sugarcane is most common in the north, around Uttar Pradesh, and in the south-west.

in-5g5P.title: Pole: concrete trident, middle insulator on top
in-5g5P.summary: On concrete poles in the south-west (Karnataka) and sometimes Haryana, the middle insulator sits on top and the other two on a crossbar slightly lower. A variant has several bars.

in-6dEm.title: Language: Devanagari script, line on top of words
in-6dEm.summary: Hindi is the most common language, in central and northern areas. Its Devanagari script has a line along the top of each word and many straight vertical strokes.

in-71TX.title: Pole: concrete poles with holes
in-71TX.summary: Concrete poles with holes are unique to the west coast state (Gujarat) and two nearby union territories. Rare in neighbouring states. Holey poles take priority over other pole clues.

in-8xSH.title: Pole: two crossbars with side supports, diagonal braces
in-8xSH.summary: In the east (West Bengal), pole tops with two crossbars joined by thin vertical supports on each side, with the lower bar braced by diagonals to the pole.

in-9N7d.title: Plants: date palms in dry central regions
in-9N7d.summary: Date palms are common in drier central areas, where there are fewer tropical and coastal palms.

in-9Tsu.title: Landscape: snow massif with three peaks, middle tallest
in-9Tsu.summary: Chaukhamba, near Ukhimath, is a snow-covered massif with three distinct peaks. The centre one is the tallest.

in-AFUm.title: Vehicles: large square-shaped cars
in-AFUm.summary: Large, visible square-shaped cars appear in the areas on the map. A similar car with a visible hood exists in Odisha.

in-AOWS.title: Landscape: by far the tallest mountains in the north
in-AOWS.summary: The tallest mountains by far are in the Himalayas.

in-Cjpf.title: Roads: separated middle bus lanes
in-Cjpf.summary: On big roads in two western cities there are separated middle lanes for buses, though people often drive in them anyway.

in-Coga.title: Pole: upside-down triangle top below the pole top
in-Coga.summary: Upside-down triangle pole tops, placed below the top of the pole, are common in the west and centre (Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh) and less often Madhya Pradesh.

in-DSvA.title: Language: Devanagari-like script without top line
in-DSvA.summary: In the west (Gujarat), the script is similar to Hindi but has no horizontal line along the top of words.

in-DXqu.title: Google car: low-quality brownish camera, round blur
in-DXqu.summary: Most coverage uses a low-quality camera with brownish colours and often a big round blur over the car. Nepal is entirely like this; Cambodia often, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh rarely.

in-DjKX.title: Google car: Gen 4 smallcam, low with big blur
in-DjKX.summary: Gen 4 coverage was filmed with the smallcam, mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through and hard to spot.

in-EI08.title: Pole: one black stripe between two white
in-EI08.summary: Markings on poles and trees of one black stripe between two white ones are common in the far south (Tamil Nadu).

in-EN0e.title: Language: Devanagari with the letter ळ
in-EN0e.summary: In the west (Maharashtra), the language also uses Devanagari, but sometimes has the letter ळ, which Hindi lacks.

in-EpYR.title: Landscape: snowy mountains, brown grass, hanging pines
in-EpYR.summary: One far north-east valley (Mechuka) is the only place in the north-east with snowy mountains, with brownish grass and many Bhutan white pines. North of it the coverage turns overcast and dark.

differs.how: Bhutan white pine also grows near Bhutan border

in-F2x8.title: Language: Bengali script plus ৰ and ৱ
in-F2x8.summary: In the north-east (Assam), the Bengali script is used with extra characters, notably ৰ and ৱ.

in-FXS4.title: Pole: upside-down trapezoid connector
in-FXS4.summary: An upside-down trapezoid connector is most common in the centre-east (Chhattisgarh), fairly common in a few north-east states and the west, and rare elsewhere. Use it only if no other pole clue shows.

in-FkZ8.title: Pole: small yellow markings
in-FkZ8.summary: Small yellow pole markings are common in the south-west (Kerala). Similar stickers rarely appear in other states.

in-Ha4e.title: Plants: tree trunks with four red-white stripes
in-Ha4e.summary: Trees with four red and white stripes near the bottom are found in the north-east plains (Bihar) and less commonly Jharkhand.

in-Ib52.title: Vehicles: taxis with yellow hood or yellow circle
in-Ib52.summary: In the Himalayan north-east (Sikkim), taxis often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.

in-J22J.title: Language: Latin-script Mizo
in-J22J.summary: In the north-east (Mizoram), the main language other than English is Mizo, written in the Latin alphabet.

in-JCqV.title: Google car: many Gen 3 walkers among poor camera
in-JCqV.summary: Most coverage is poor quality, but lots of Gen 3 walker (backpack) coverage is spread across the country.

in-JQjD.title: Pole: two crossbars, each with two insulators
in-JQjD.summary: In the north-east (Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram), poles often have two crossbars with two insulators each. More than two bars means Meghalaya or Mizoram. Rare elsewhere.

in-LNOp.title: Landscape: plateau-topped ridges of the western mountains
in-LNOp.summary: The Western Ghats in western Maharashtra have distinct ridgelines, often plateaus not peaks. The north is drier, the south greener. In the rainy season they turn green.

in-MbN7.title: Pole: trident top on all-metal poles
in-MbN7.summary: In the far north-east (Manipur), trident tops sit on all-metal poles, sometimes with small bars on top of the trident.

in-N2o3.title: Landscape: lush valleys, eroded hills with small peaks
in-N2o3.summary: In the far north-east (Mizoram), lush green valleys with low plants and eroded hillsides with many small peaks. Meghalaya is similar, but its hills have smooth flat tops instead of peaks.

in-OA5s.title: Houses: thatched roofs, hay mounds in the east
in-OA5s.summary: Thatched houses or huts are mainly along the east coast and northern plains, with large hay mounds. From the north to the east they use fine hay; from the east to the far south, dried palm fans.

in-OQp6.title: Landscape: flat bushy land with very red soil
in-OQp6.summary: South of Tamil Nadu has flat, bushy land with very red soil.

in-OsUg.title: Plants: very thin palm trunk with small crown
in-OsUg.summary: Areca palms have very thin trunks and small crowns. Mostly on the south-west coast, the north-east and the Andaman and Nicobar islands.

in-Q9xQ.title: Houses: white-painted clay huts
in-Q9xQ.summary: White-painted clay huts are found in the north-west of Bihar and north-east of Uttar Pradesh.

in-RBjJ.title: Houses: bright orange flat tiles with middle ridge
in-RBjJ.summary: In the south, roofs have tidy, bright orange flat tiles with a ridge in the middle, especially in the far south. Similar darker brown tiles are common further north.

in-RdbC.title: Crops: oil palm plantations in the south-east
in-RdbC.summary: Oil palm plantations are most common in the eastern panhandle of Andhra Pradesh, especially near the Telangana border.

in-RjU1.title: Signs: planned city, sector and numbered streets
in-RjU1.summary: A planned industrial city has blue signs naming sectors and industrial areas, round yellow marks on street lights, and street signs with several numbers instead of names. Two nearby planned cities have similar signs.

in-TTvA.title: Language: Meitei script, vertical lines and right angles
in-TTvA.summary: In the north-east (Manipur), Meitei script has many vertical lines and right angles.

in-TUVo.title: Plants: chir pines, smooth cone crowns, very long needles
in-TUVo.summary: Chir pines grow almost only in the Himalayan north and the far west of the north-east. They have smooth conical or round crowns and very long needles.

in-TlL9.title: Pole: short crossbar above longer crossbar
in-TlL9.summary: Pole tops with a short crossbar above a longer one are found on the west coast (Goa).

in-WJAr.title: Language: simple curvy letters with upside-down U shapes
in-WJAr.summary: In the south-west (Kerala), the script is mostly simple, curvy letters, often with upside-down U shapes.

in-XHTM.title: Landscape: extremely dry Himalaya, no vegetation
in-XHTM.summary: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh, the Himalayas are extremely dry with almost no plants.

in-XLIO.title: Road: khasi pines, yellow edge lines, fresh dark tarmac
in-XLIO.summary: Parts of NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong have khasi pines, yellow outer lines and fresh dark asphalt. It is the only road in Meghalaya with yellow edge lines, but other states have them too.

in-YMCx.title: Crops: canola in the north-west
in-YMCx.summary: Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.

in-ZCB2.title: Plants: carnivorous pitcher plants by the road
in-ZCB2.summary: The endangered Indian pitcher plant lives only in the Khasi Hills (Meghalaya). You may spot it by the road, especially on NH206 north of one village.

in-ZN7M.title: Landscape: huge monolithic rock mountains
in-ZN7M.summary: Near the far southern tip, large monolithic mountains with huge exposed rock, visible from afar, especially the Mahendragiri hills.

in-aEYi.title: Language: many different scripts
in-aEYi.summary: Many scripts are used across the country, and most help you narrow down the region.

in-ahUu.title: Pole: thin grey metal poles, often two together
in-ahUu.summary: Thin grey metal poles, often two next to each other, are common across the north-east and the Himalayan north (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh).

in-b5Ry.title: Language: curves, straight lines and 90-degree angles
in-b5Ry.summary: In the far south (Tamil Nadu), the script mixes curves, straight lines and right angles, and some letters have dot marks. Tamil is also common in Sri Lanka.

in-cIYN.title: Houses: rounded roof tiles, messy rows
in-cIYN.summary: Rounded roof tiles are common in central India, often laid untidily in not quite straight rows and columns.

in-creX.title: Landscape: dry sandy western desert
in-creX.summary: The west of Rajasthan is dry with sandy soil.

in-dvg8.title: Decor: Buddhist prayer flags
in-dvg8.summary: Buddhist prayer flags are found in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

in-ex3H.title: Language: Bengali script, left-facing triangles
in-ex3H.summary: In the north-east, the script is like Devanagari but with many letters featuring left-facing triangles. Bangladesh uses the same language.

in-f8wS.title: Houses: wooden huts with cross pattern
in-f8wS.summary: Wooden huts with a cross pattern are found in the centre of Bihar.

in-hONE.title: Language: softer script, broken top line, ਨ ਲ ਅ
in-hONE.summary: In the north-west (Punjab), the script resembles Hindi but is softer, with a top bar broken over some letters. Look for ਨ, ਲ, ਅ and a soft curved mark under a letter.

in-idcC.title: Pole: tall narrow rectangle pole top
in-idcC.summary: Pole tops attached with two vertical bars forming a tall, narrow rectangle are found in the east (West Bengal).

in-jEYq.title: Plants: tall Japanese cedars with narrow fluffy crowns
in-jEYq.summary: Japanese cedars are very tall with narrow fluffy crowns. Most common near the border of Sikkim and West Bengal, and in Meghalaya.

in-jOuK.title: Pole: metal poles with mesh pattern
in-jOuK.summary: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are common in the Himalayan north-east (Sikkim).

in-joq6.title: Language: almost only English, north-east hills
in-joq6.summary: English appears everywhere, but one north-east state (Meghalaya) uses it almost exclusively.

in-ju41.title: Crops: tea plantations in north-east and far south
in-ju41.summary: Tea plantations are found in the north-east and the far south. Tea on flat ground means Assam or north-east West Bengal.

in-kBP5.title: Fences: thin wooden sticks in square pattern
in-kBP5.summary: In the north-east, fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern are common.

in-lI6D.title: Plants: lollipop-shaped palms
in-lI6D.summary: Palmyra palms have a round crown of fan leaves on a trunk of even thickness, like a lollipop. Many of them mean the south or east.

in-lQsr.title: Plants: Khasi pines, jagged crowns
in-lQsr.summary: Khasi pines are mainly in two north-east states (Meghalaya, Manipur). Needles look like chir pine but the crown is more jagged and messy.

in-lRZg.title: Landscape: barren brown hills on the Himalayan edge
in-lRZg.summary: The west of Uttarakhand is much more barren than other Himalayan areas due to logging and erosion. North-west of Dehradun there are barren hills of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

in-lVvh.title: Houses: roofs of thin grey bricks near a state border
in-lVvh.summary: Near the border of two southern states (Telangana, Karnataka), roofs often use thin grey bricks, and similar grey rocks appear in walls and scattered in stockyards.

in-lduR.title: Pole: small window-shaped metal pole tops
in-lduR.summary: Small window-shaped metal pole tops are found in the north-west (Punjab, Haryana).

in-ljSa.title: Language: round curvy script, squiggly tails
in-ljSa.summary: In the south (Karnataka), the script has smooth curves and small circles, close to Telugu. Many letters have a squiggly tail in the top right, less common in Telugu.

in-lm-128926.title: Landscape: dry land between two southern towns
in-lm-128926.summary: With a Telangana or Andhra pole or Telugu text and dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur and Shadnagar.

in-lm-128927.title: Landscape: flat red soil on the east coast
in-lm-128927.summary: Andhra Pradesh has a long east coast. Flat land with red soil and lots of palmyra palms almost always means the eastern coast of India.

in-lm-128928.title: Landscape: flat farmland with coastal bushes
in-lm-128928.summary: Coastal Andhra Pradesh is flat farmland with coastal bushes. Gujarat has similar bushes, but also holey poles or boxy cars and mostly date palms; Andhra has palmyra palms. Rounds with no palms or poles can be a 50/50 with other flat, farmed states.

in-lm-128929.title: Landscape: rocky desert in a valley
in-lm-128929.summary: A rocky desert in a valley south-west of Nandyala in Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-128930.title: Bridges: red-orange vertical blocks with white horizontals
in-lm-128930.summary: Bridges in two south-east states often have red, pink or orange vertical concrete blocks with horizontal white or light yellow ones.

in-lm-128931.title: Landscape: huge ridge to the north of a city
in-lm-128931.summary: One south-eastern city is easy to recognise by a huge ridge to the north. Confirm with black-and-yellow tuk-tuks, two-indent poles, or the local language.

in-lm-149565.title: Houses: thatched roofs in three areas of the south-east
in-lm-149565.summary: In Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs are mainly south-east of Guntur, then south of Nellore, where a rare red car appears, and sparsely around Srikakulam.

in-lm-149566.title: Pole: green stripes in the far west of the north-east
in-lm-149566.summary: Green stripes on poles are common on the far west roads of Arunachal Pradesh, often with yellow or white stripes.

in-lm-149567.title: Pole: white numbers on blue, red or black paint
in-lm-149567.summary: A section of NH13 west of Roing has poles with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.

in-lm-149568.title: Bollard: rare red and white bollards
in-lm-149568.summary: Red-and-white bollards are quite rare, mostly in far west Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-149569.title: Bollard: rare black bollards in far north-east
in-lm-149569.summary: Black bollards are rare and not unique, but in Arunachal Pradesh they are most common in the far west, north of two towns, and on route 319 in the east.

in-lm-149570.title: Road: only divided road in the north-east state
in-lm-149570.summary: The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar.

in-lm-149571.title: Google car: unique car in a high valley
in-lm-149571.summary: One valley in Arunachal Pradesh has a unique car, also on the NH13 road leading to it from Along.

in-lm-149572.title: Google car: white car with mirrors west of a capital
in-lm-149572.summary: In Arunachal Pradesh, a white car with mirrors is found on the road west of Itanagar.

in-lm-149573.title: Google car: white boxy car between two towns
in-lm-149573.summary: A white, boxy-looking car in Arunachal Pradesh means the road between Tezu and Lohitpur.

in-lm-149574.title: Google car: black and red cars in one town
in-lm-149574.summary: In Arunachal Pradesh, both a black and a red car appear only around Roing. The black one is mainly on NH313 and east; the red one mainly west of the main road.

in-lm-149575.title: Google car: back antenna near two spots
in-lm-149575.summary: In Arunachal Pradesh, a back antenna shows up around Chowkam and east of Namsai.

in-lm-289866.title: Google car: yellow car in a small mountain state
in-lm-289866.summary: In Sikkim, starting at Rangpo, a noticeable yellow car appears. It may have an antenna, be blurred, or almost invisible, but a yellow car means you are here.

in-lm-289956.title: Pole: yellow bands between two towns
in-lm-289956.summary: On the NH6 between Aizawl and Champhai, poles have yellow bands.

in-lm-289969.title: Landscape: snow at the end of very high roads
in-lm-289969.summary: Coverage reaches very high-altitude roads, so snow can show at the end of the coverage east of Leh.

in-lm-289970.title: Google car: antenna on top left, far west of a hill state
in-lm-289970.summary: In the very far west of Meghalaya, on roads north of Purakhasia, a car has an antenna on the top left that is hard to see.

in-lm-289971.title: Landscape: hilly forest with areca palms around flat fields
in-lm-289971.summary: West Meghalaya looks like Bangladesh with hills: lots of areca palms, banana trees and palms, hilly forests around flat farmland.

differs.how: Western Meghalaya looks like Bangladesh with hills

in-lm-289972.title: Road: only divided highway in a hill state
in-lm-289972.summary: The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya. Another tell for that state is the lack of non-Latin scripts.

in-lm-289973.title: Landscape: farm fields in a valley ringed by mountains
in-lm-289973.summary: The capital of Manipur sits in a valley, so the landscape is farm fields surrounded by mountains. Easy to recognise after a few rounds.

in-lm-289974.title: Google car: long antenna with black car front
in-lm-289974.summary: In Mizoram, a long antenna with a black car front means the NH6 north of Serkhan. This car is not unique to Mizoram.

in-lm-289975.title: Google car: black front, stubby antenna
in-lm-289975.summary: In Mizoram, a car with a black front and stubby antenna is on roads west of Aizawl.

in-lm-289976.title: Google car: grey car with double mirrors
in-lm-289976.summary: In Mizoram, a grey car with double mirrors appears in the southernmost coverage near NH502.

in-lm-289977.title: Bridges: blue and white concrete blocks
in-lm-289977.summary: Bridges in West Bengal often have blue and white concrete blocks. Rarely also in Bihar around Gaya.

in-lm-289978.title: Google car: white car with visible front
in-lm-289978.summary: All roads in Ladakh show this white car with a visible front.

in-lm-306065.title: Landscape: huge mountains with slightly greener slopes
in-lm-306065.summary: This section of NH3 between Gramphu and Dala has huge mountains with a bit more green on their slopes.

in-lm-306066.title: Landscape: very dry, very high, sparse-green valley
in-lm-306066.summary: A valley whose mountains are very dry, very high and sparsely green. If you confuse it with the NH3 to the west, know that NH3 is paved while roads in this valley usually are not.

in-lm-306141.title: Houses: lots of bright green and red roofs
in-lm-306141.summary: The Himalayan town of Shimla has the most bright green and bright red roofs and buildings, and also lots of Himalayan cedars.

in-lm-306142.title: Google car: white boxy car, bars and strap leaning right
in-lm-306142.summary: A white, boxy car with bars and a central strap leaning right. Mainly in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Sultanpur in Uttar Pradesh.

in-lm-306143.title: Landscape: pines on elevated land near a northern city
in-lm-306143.summary: Much of Jammu's coverage is flat, but north and north-east of the city the land rises and shows lots of pines.

in-lm-306144.title: Houses: richer-looking, developed feel
in-lm-306144.summary: The far-north city looks fairly developed with richer architecture. Punjab is similar. If rich houses show up, check the car: without one of the two boxy Jammu cars with a top-right thread or central strap, click Punjab.

in-lm-306145.title: Landscape: town in a north-south mountain valley
in-lm-306145.summary: One mountain town is one of two areas with coverage in a recognisable north-south valley; the other runs from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south. Poplars and pines inside the town are one way to tell them apart.

in-lm-306146.title: Guardrail: only double guardrail road in the state
in-lm-306146.summary: The NH5 near Sarahan is the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.

in-lm-306147.title: Google car: boxy car only in the mountain-state capital
in-lm-306147.summary: Only one city in Himachal Pradesh has the boxy car, with its top right corner visible through a thread, sometimes not visible.

in-lm-397.title: Pole: small yellow markings
in-lm-397.summary: Small yellow pole markings are common in the south-west (Kerala). Other states have them only rarely.

in-lm-402.title: Electricity box: mint green with window squares
in-lm-402.summary: Mint green electricity boxes with small window-like squares are almost only in the north-west (Punjab), rarely in Haryana.

in-lm-436099.title: Crops: sugarcane in one part of the north-east state
in-lm-436099.summary: In Assam, sugarcane is mainly found around Lanka.

in-lm-436100.title: Crops: corn between two towns, south of the river
in-lm-436100.summary: In Assam, corn is found between Guwahati and Nagaon, south of the river.

in-lm-436101.title: Houses: thatched roofs in the far north-east of Assam
in-lm-436101.summary: In Assam, thatched roofs are found all the way in the north-east of the state.

in-lm-436102.title: Google car: back antenna in the far east
in-lm-436102.summary: A back antenna in Assam means the far east of the state.

in-lm-436103.title: Houses: woven walls near the northern border
in-lm-436103.summary: In Assam, houses with woven walls appear along the Arunachal Pradesh border north of Tinsukia.

in-lm-436104.title: Bollard: black with colored stripes
in-lm-436104.summary: A black bollard with stripes, usually at least one of red, white or orange, found in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.

in-lm-436105.title: Pole: red-yellow striped poles and striped black bollards
in-lm-436105.summary: On the road south of Harsil, lots of poles with red and yellow stripes and black striped bollards.

in-lm-436106.title: Pole: orange stickers on metal poles
in-lm-436106.summary: Orange stickers on metal poles are found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the east.

in-lm-436108.title: Pole: blue stickers on metal poles
in-lm-436108.summary: Blue stickers on metal poles are found on the NH109 near Lohali.

in-lm-436109.title: Pole: yellow-black striped poles in mountains
in-lm-436109.summary: In Uttarakhand, the Bihar-style yellow-and-black pole is found on the NH109 north and a small road south of Dwarahat. Since the area is mountainous, don't mistake it for Bihar.

in-lm-436110.title: Pole: red-white stripes around one town
in-lm-436110.summary: Red and white stripes on poles are found on random roads around Dwarahat in Uttarakhand.

in-lm-436111.title: Sticker: round white stickers all over a city
in-lm-436111.summary: Round white stickers are found all over Dehradun.

in-lm-436112.title: Google car: red boxy car in an inverted V
in-lm-436112.summary: In Punjab, the red boxy car is found in Ludhiana, Chandigarh and a bit north between them. The coverage forms an inverted V.

in-lm-436113.title: Google car: black boxy car on the western border
in-lm-436113.summary: In Punjab, the black boxy car is on the Pakistani border between Firozpur and Amritsar.

in-lm-436114.title: Landscape: hills in an otherwise very flat state
in-lm-436114.summary: Punjab is very flat. If you know you are in Punjab but it is hilly, you are on the border with Himachal Pradesh.

in-lm-436115.title: Google car: forest car only in one forest
in-lm-436115.summary: In Punjab, this car is only in the Dasuya forest, but it also exists outside Punjab.

in-lm-436116.title: Google car: boxy car with rounded front
in-lm-436116.summary: This car is unique to one place in Punjab. It resembles the boxy car but has a rounded front.

in-lm-436117.title: Landscape: very green, lush farmland, much sugarcane
in-lm-436117.summary: Northern Haryana is very green and agricultural. The Ganges valley looks like this too, but this area is greener, lusher and has more sugarcane.

in-lm-436118.title: Landscape: farmland that still looks dry
in-lm-436118.summary: Southern Haryana and southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural but often look dry, like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

in-lm-436119.title: Landscape: drier look than neighbours
in-lm-436119.summary: Rajasthan is drier than the states around it. Many places simply have a drier feel that is hard to explain.

in-lm-436120.title: Ads: man with turban and beard, hexagon logo
in-lm-436120.summary: In Bihar and Jharkhand, many ads show a man with a turban and beard, usually with a hexagonal company logo on yellow. Copycats exist with other logos, so don't trust it blindly.

in-lm-436121.title: Houses: regular wide W tiles in one town area
in-lm-436121.summary: In Bihar, regular wide W tiles are found around Katihar. They resemble W tiles but larger, with a small spike in the middle.

in-lm-436122.title: Houses: orange and black wide W tiles
in-lm-436122.summary: Orange and black wide W tiles probably mean around Madhubani in Bihar.

in-lm-436123.title: Houses: huts made entirely of hay
in-lm-436123.summary: Huts made entirely of hay with thatched roofs are found in south-west Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.

in-lm-436124.title: Houses: tin hip roofs in the north-east of the state
in-lm-436124.summary: Tin hip roofs, usually found in West Bengal, mean the north-east quarter of Bihar.

in-lm-436125.title: Houses: clay houses
in-lm-436125.summary: Clay houses are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, with some spill into far south-west Bihar.

in-lm-436126.title: Houses: clay-plastered woven walls near the border
in-lm-436126.summary: Woven walls plastered with clay are found on the west half of the Bihar-Nepal border.

differs.how: Woven clay walls near the Nepal border

in-lm-436127.title: Pole: black-yellow-black pole paint along the river
in-lm-436127.summary: The black-yellow-black pole paint, also famous in a Colombian region, is found in east Bihar along the Ganges.

in-lm-436128.title: Crops: pineapple in the corridor between two countries
in-lm-436128.summary: Pineapple is very uncommon, but if you see it, it is in Bihar, in the corridor between Nepal and Bangladesh.

in-lm-436129.title: Crops: tea plantations in the far north-east of Bihar
in-lm-436129.summary: In Bihar, tea plantations are in the far north-east.

in-lm-436130.title: Landscape: mountains to the north on the border
in-lm-436130.summary: In Assam, mountains to the north mean the border with Arunachal Pradesh, especially east of Itanagar.

in-lm-436131.title: Landscape: hilliness south and east of a town
in-lm-436131.summary: Hilliness in Assam is mostly south or east of Nagaon.

in-lm-436132.title: Plants: white roadside flowers in three areas
in-lm-436132.summary: In Assam, white flowers often line the road in three areas: the border with West Bengal, the border with eastern Bhutan, and west of Nagaon.

in-lm-436133.title: Google car: white car with black-and-grey side bar
in-lm-436133.summary: A white car characterised by a black and grey bar on the side, found only in Goa.

in-lm-443923.title: Landscape: north-east angled ridge
in-lm-443923.summary: In Rajasthan, a ridge runs north-east from the Mount Abu area to New Delhi.

in-lm-443924.title: Landscape: rolling hills south of a city
in-lm-443924.summary: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common south of Udaipur.

in-lm-443925.title: Landscape: the biggest mountains in the dry west state
in-lm-443925.summary: The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar in the far north-east and the Udaipur-Mount Abu area.

in-lm-443926.title: Plants: narrow hills with lots of euphorbia cacti
in-lm-443926.summary: South of Udaipur, a distinct landscape of narrow hills with lots of euphorbia cactus.

in-lm-443927.title: Plants: euphorbia cacti on flat land
in-lm-443927.summary: West of Mount Abu, lots of euphorbia cacti in flat land. Euphorbia appears in other states like Gujarat too.

in-lm-443928.title: Plants: calotropis shrubs everywhere
in-lm-443928.summary: Calotropis procera grows all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states, so lots of it is a good Rajasthan clue.

in-lm-443929.title: Walls: stone walls, hilly south or flat south-east
in-lm-443929.summary: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you are there, they are most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and south-east of Kota (flat).

in-lm-443930.title: Road: concrete road with yellow lines
in-lm-443930.summary: From Sukma to the Andhra Pradesh border, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete, a bit like Chile's Ruta 9.

in-lm-443932.title: Walls: rock walls around two national parks
in-lm-443932.summary: In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around Kuno and Panna national parks.

in-lm-443933.title: Crops: sugarcane south-west and north-east of a park
in-lm-443933.summary: In Madhya Pradesh, sugarcane is common south-west and north-east of Satpura National Park.

in-lm-443935.title: Landscape: hilly with dead trees
in-lm-443935.summary: A unique hilly landscape with dead trees in a wildlife sanctuary. Not all coverage in the park looks like this.

in-lm-443936.title: Landscape: where the centre has elevation
in-lm-443936.summary: Elevation in Madhya Pradesh is mainly around Yawal and Satpura park and south of Indore.

in-lm-443937.title: Landscape: straight east-west ridge near one town
in-lm-443937.summary: A fairly straight east-west mountain range with a slight north-east angle near Rewa, easy to recognise.

in-lm-443938.title: Houses: rare W tiles in the centre
in-lm-443938.summary: W tiles are rare in Madhya Pradesh but seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna.

in-lm-443939.title: Houses: U tiles in the east half
in-lm-443939.summary: U tiles are more common in the east half of Madhya Pradesh.

in-lm-443940.title: Houses: flat tiles in central towns
in-lm-443940.summary: Flat tiles show up randomly in Madhya Pradesh but mostly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar.

in-lm-443941.title: Houses: slate roofs west of one town
in-lm-443941.summary: Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh are found west of Sagar.

in-lm-451240.title: Houses: tiled roofs with blue painted walls
in-lm-451240.summary: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a bit less in Madhya Pradesh.

in-lm-451241.title: Houses: long tiled roofs, two-tone walls
in-lm-451241.summary: Between Dumka and Pakur, houses have long tiled roofs and walls painted in two colours: green or blue with orange or brown at the bottom.

in-lm-451243.title: Houses: wide W tiles spilling into the east
in-lm-451243.summary: In eastern Jharkhand, some wide W tiles spill over from West Bengal.

in-lm-451244.title: Structures: elevated structures between two cities
in-lm-451244.summary: These elevated structures appear a lot between Hazaribagh and Ranchi.

in-lm-451245.title: Google car: car with an orange flag
in-lm-451245.summary: A car with an orange flag is found in the north-east panhandle of Jharkhand.

in-lm-451246.title: Plants: many date palms mixed with palmyra palms
in-lm-451246.summary: In Jharkhand you very often see lots of date palms together with palmyra palms, one of the best clues for it. Telangana has the same mix, so look for text.

in-lm-451247.title: Crops: sugarcane mostly in the centre
in-lm-451247.summary: Sugarcane in Maharashtra is mostly in the centre.

in-lm-451248.title: Crops: grapes, by far the top producer
in-lm-451248.summary: Maharashtra grows by far the most grapes in India.

in-lm-451250.title: Crops: cotton in the middle and east, unreliable
in-lm-451250.summary: Cotton is mostly around Nanded and more broadly the middle and east of Maharashtra. Very unreliable.

in-lm-474781.title: Houses: only W tiles, not in the south
in-lm-474781.summary: The only roof tile type in Telangana is the W tile, and it does not go into the south of the state.

in-lm-474782.title: Landscape: rocky roadsides, boulders and rocky slopes
in-lm-474782.summary: Telangana and Andhra Pradesh have lots of rockiness: rocks beside the road, boulders, rocky slopes. More in Telangana, and extends into Karnataka and Andhra. In Andhra it is common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.

in-lm-474783.title: Crops: cotton in the north-west
in-lm-474783.summary: Cotton in Telangana is mainly in the north-west, next to Maharashtra's big cotton area. Click near Nizamabad, or north of it.

in-lm-474784.title: Google car: black car more common here
in-lm-474784.summary: Not common, but a black car is more likely in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, especially northern Telangana and coastal Andhra.

in-lm-474785.title: Plants: coconut palms in the south-east towards the coast
in-lm-474785.summary: Coconut palms are more common in the south-east half of Telangana towards Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-474787.title: Google car: black car with black side bars
in-lm-474787.summary: A black car with black bars on each side, found only in Goa.

in-lm-474788.title: Houses: colorful, especially blue, walls
in-lm-474788.summary: Houses with colourful, especially blue, painted walls are found around eastern Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

in-lm-474790.title: Roads: long straight highway under construction
in-lm-474790.summary: In 2025 a large part of the NH-66 in Kerala is under construction, so a long straight highway with roadworks in smallcam is likely this road.

in-lm-506099.title: Google car: back-curving bar, mostly blurred
in-lm-506099.summary: This car has a back-curving bar and is mostly blurred. Found east of Kuno National Park.

in-lm-506100.title: Google car: back-curving bar and one black bar
in-lm-506100.summary: This car has a back-curving bar and a single black bar. Mainly east of Satpura National Park, sometimes around Raipura.

in-lm-506101.title: Google car: curving front bar, white side bars
in-lm-506101.summary: This car has a back-curving bar at the front and white bars on the sides. Mostly around Rewa, also around Raipura.

in-lm-506132.title: Houses: thatched roofs along the east coast
in-lm-506132.summary: Thatched roofs are all over the east coast. In Odisha they are mostly between Balasore and Puri, but also inland and in the south-west. Thatch alone suggests the coast.

in-lm-506133.title: Houses: U tiles in the north-west of the state
in-lm-506133.summary: In Odisha, U tiles are common in the north-west, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh.

in-lm-506134.title: Bridges: green and white concrete block guardrails
in-lm-506134.summary: Some bridges in Odisha have green and white concrete blocks as guardrails.

in-lm-506135.title: Houses: often painted green
in-lm-506135.summary: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.

in-lm-506136.title: Houses: W tiles in two areas
in-lm-506136.summary: In Odisha, W-tiled roofs are found in a corridor north of Bhubaneswar and in the south-west, south-west of Bhawanipatna.

in-lm-506138.title: Google car: boxy car with 6 indents
in-lm-506138.summary: A boxy car with 6 indents is found near Malkangiri in Odisha.

in-lm-506139.title: Houses: U tiles mixed with W tiles near one town
in-lm-506139.summary: When mixed with W tiles, U tiles are most common around Umerkote.

in-lm-506141.title: Google car: car with flowers on the front
in-lm-506141.summary: A car with flowers on the front is found around Keonjhar, on routes 49 and 20.

in-lm-506142.title: Google car: boxy car with 5 indents
in-lm-506142.summary: A boxy car with 5 indents is found near the Subarnarekha river mouth at the Odisha-West Bengal border.

in-lm-506143.title: Symbols: shell, a regional party logo
in-lm-506143.summary: The shell is the symbol of an Odisha-specific political party, the Biju Janata Dal.

in-lm-506144.title: Vehicles: black tuk-tuks (maybe fake)
in-lm-506144.summary: Black tuk-tuks are most common in Maharashtra, possibly a fake meta.

in-lm-506145.title: Landscape: much greener panhandle with many coconuts
in-lm-506145.summary: The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks different from the rest of the state: much greener, darker, and with far more coconut palms. Other areas have palmyra palms. The area south of Tirupati can look extremely similar but has less coverage.

in-lm-506146.title: Plants: dead-looking trees
in-lm-506146.summary: These dead-looking trees are a strong sign of Rajasthan, concentrated mostly south-west of Sikar.

in-lm-506147.title: Google car: open trunk in smallcam
in-lm-506147.summary: In the east of Ajmer in Rajasthan, you can sometimes see an open trunk in smallcam, north of Shrinagar and west of Circular Rd.

in-lm-512392.title: Plants: tall narrow teak forest in wet season
in-lm-512392.summary: Teak forests in wet season with the boxy car are around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are tall and narrow.

in-lm-512583.title: Google car: boxy car only around one big city
in-lm-512583.summary: In Karnataka, the boxy car is only in and around Bengaluru.

in-lm-512584.title: Houses: W tiles mean the west or south-west
in-lm-512584.summary: A W-tiled roof in Karnataka means you can go to the west or south-west part of the state.

in-lm-512585.title: Houses: slate roofs between two cities
in-lm-512585.summary: Slate roofs are in a specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad, the same area as the thin grey stones, so often seen together.

in-lm-512586.title: Bollard: red reflector on a stone bollard
in-lm-512586.summary: These bollards are unique for the red reflector on a stone bollard.

in-lm-512587.title: Bridges: blue and white, sometimes green
in-lm-512587.summary: Blue and white bridges are common all over Kerala, sometimes painted green.

in-lm-512588.title: Symbols: communist flags and party symbols
in-lm-512588.summary: Communist symbols are mostly in Kerala, then much less in Tamil Nadu, sometimes in Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, and rarely elsewhere. The party youth wing, DYFI, shows the same pattern.

in-lm-512589.title: Google car: antenna car, west coast and island
in-lm-512589.summary: This car, with an antenna, is found in Goa and in the union territory of Daman.

in-lm-512591.title: Google car: car with a rear spoiler
in-lm-512591.summary: A car with a spoiler at the back, found in the far north of the Andaman islands near Diglipur.

in-lm-512592.title: Pole: horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole
in-lm-512592.summary: Pole tops in the Andamans mostly are horizontal bars across the pole. Not 100% unique, but very common there.

in-lm-512593.title: Coverage: remote islands, oversaturated colours
in-lm-512593.summary: The Andamans are remote islands with their own vegetation, covered in areca palm forests and very thin roads. The camera had maxed saturation, giving very bright, whitish colours.

in-lm-520192.title: Google car: mostly blurred, faint white front edges
in-lm-520192.summary: This car is mostly blurred with subtle white edges at the front, found on the island of Agatti. It can be confused with Kalpeni's car, which has a subtle black blur.

in-lm-520193.title: Google car: white front with black stripes
in-lm-520193.summary: The car front is white with black stripes, sometimes a visible side mirror and a bar at the back. Exclusive to the island of Amini.

in-lm-520194.title: Google car: big circular blur on two islands
in-lm-520194.summary: A big circular blur, solid or transparent, is common with older cameras. In Lakshadweep it only shows on Andrott and Kalpeni, which also each have a unique car.

in-lm-520195.title: Google car: red front blur
in-lm-520195.summary: The red front blur is on Andrott, sometimes with some exposed red. Andrott can also show the big blur with no car.

in-lm-520196.title: Google car: exposed white front, no mirror
in-lm-520196.summary: A car with an exposed white front on Kadmat. If a side mirror shows or the front is blurred, it is not this car.

in-lm-520197.title: Google car: white front with left mirror showing
in-lm-520197.summary: The most likely Lakshadweep car: white front, always a bit of left mirror visible. It is common because it is on the main island, Kavaratti.

in-lm-520198.title: Google car: exposed black front
in-lm-520198.summary: A car with an exposed black front, unique to Kiltan. The front is always exposed; if blurred even partly, it is not this car.

in-lm-520199.title: Google car: subtle black blur at front
in-lm-520199.summary: A car with a subtle black blur at the front, on Kalpeni. The blur can be very faint and confusable with Agatti's white edges. Kalpeni can also show a big round blur.

in-lm-520200.title: Landscape: mountains along the western edge
in-lm-520200.summary: In Tamil Nadu, mountains are along the western border, plenty west of Madurai and some east of Salem.

in-lm-520201.title: Pole: 3 insulators in a line
in-lm-520201.summary: Three insulators in a horizontal line, or the middle one slightly higher. About 88% Tamil Nadu, 5% Bihar, 3% Haryana.

in-lm-520202.title: Houses: nice houses with W tiles and bluish paint
in-lm-520202.summary: In Tamil Nadu, good-looking houses often have W-tiled roofs and bluish paint, about 95% Tamil Nadu. W tiles are everywhere but less common in the north-east and east coast, where U tiles are more common.

in-lm-520203.title: Buildings: temples with pyramid towers
in-lm-520203.summary: Southern temples have shorter pyramid-shaped towers, monumental ornate gateways and door guardian statues.

in-lm-520204.title: Houses: rare U tiles in the north-east
in-lm-520204.summary: U-tiled roofs are rare in Tamil Nadu and should be in the north-east. A few further south near Thanjavur usually come with thatched roofs.

in-lm-520205.title: Houses: thatched roofs south-east of one town
in-lm-520205.summary: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south-east of Thanjavur.

in-lm-520206.title: Walls: rare wall pattern around one city
in-lm-520206.summary: A particular wall pattern is found in and around Chennai but is rare.

in-lm-520207.title: Crops: tea in one area north-west of a city
in-lm-520207.summary: Tea is mostly in the north-east and Kerala, with some spill into one area of Tamil Nadu north-west of Coimbatore.

in-lm-520208.title: Crops: sugarcane near two northern areas
in-lm-520208.summary: In Tamil Nadu, sugarcane is mainly near Erode and Thiruvannamalai, with smaller patches between, so mainly the north.

in-lm-520209.title: Houses: elevated curved-roof style
in-lm-520209.summary: Found mostly in the southern part of West Bengal, more in the west, and sometimes in Bihar near the Nepal border. Not well researched.

differs.how: Sometimes at the border near eastern Nepal

in-lm-520210.title: Plants: prickly pear cactus (unsure)
in-lm-520210.summary: Found in Gujarat, mainly on the southern peninsula. Could be fake.

in-lm-520211.title: Plants: agave, a weak clue
in-lm-520211.summary: Agaves are mostly in Karnataka, but are found in many places and are a generally fake meta. With nothing else, Karnataka is a place to consider.

in-lm-520212.title: Plants: date palms in the north-east
in-lm-520212.summary: In Tamil Nadu, date palms are in the north-east.

in-lm-520213.title: Plants: parasol leaf trees on the south-west coast
in-lm-520213.summary: Parasol leaf trees are common on the south-west coast, south of Mumbai, and seem nearly exclusive there. Look for teardrop leaves where the stem joins inside the blade.

in-lm-520214.title: Google car: antenna with a spring-like part
in-lm-520214.summary: This car has an antenna with a spring-like part. It runs basically from Salem to Chennai.

in-lm-527153.title: Pole: concrete trident with three crossbars
in-lm-527153.summary: A concrete trident pole with three crossbars. Don't confuse it with the north-east triple pole, which has shorter crossbars and is metal. 98% Karnataka.

in-lm-527191.title: Pole: ordinary pole only in far west
in-lm-527191.summary: Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles appear sometimes in the very far west, near the Pakistan border.

in-lm-527197.title: Pole: trident with three-circle insulators and air between
in-lm-527197.summary: A trident pole with insulators of three circles with air between them is 98% Karnataka. Other versions are less certain.

in-lm-527240.title: Pole: two insulators each side, top sticking out
in-lm-527240.summary: Two insulators on each side with the top of the pole sticking out. Karnataka 94%, rarely Tamil Nadu or Kerala.

in-lm-527270.title: Pole: generic pole top with no bars on top
in-lm-527270.summary: Generic poles are typically not found south of the Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha line, except in Kerala. A generic pole top has no bars on top.

in-lm-527403.title: Pole: mesh pole in the dry west
in-lm-527403.summary: Found 90% in Rajasthan. Sikkim and Telangana also have mesh poles: the Sikkim pole is slimmer, the Telangana one has triangles at the top.

in-lm-548782.title: Landscape: lots of farming plus many palms
in-lm-548782.summary: Around Guntur, a landscape combining the green panhandle and the farmed east coast to the south: more agriculture than the panhandle and more palms than the coast.

in-lm-548829.title: Pole: trapezoid top on all-dark-metal pole
in-lm-548829.summary: Trapezoid pole tops on poles entirely of dark metal are in Chhattisgarh 95% of the time. If not dark metal, less certain.

in-lm-548830.title: Pole: trident top with V bars and window top
in-lm-548830.summary: A trident pole top with V-shaped bars underneath and a window-like top. Very specific to some roads in Chandigarh.

in-lm-548831.title: Pole: thick grey trapezoid
in-lm-548831.summary: Commonly found in Kerala, especially with yellow stickers. A version with two indents is not in Kerala but in Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-548832.title: Pole: two-section pole with bar high up
in-lm-548832.summary: Two-section poles can be regionguessed by the bar above the crossbar. If it is high, barely any concrete above it, it is 80% Telangana, 20% Andhra Pradesh. Can be hard to tell.

in-lm-548834.title: Pole: thick grey trapezoid with two indents
in-lm-548834.summary: A thick grey trapezoid with two indents in the pole material. 97% Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-548835.title: Sticker: simple black sticker with few characters
in-lm-548835.summary: A black sticker with a few characters, often just a number. About 35% Tamil Nadu, 35% Andhra Pradesh, 20% Telangana. Weak for Andhra over Telangana. Don't confuse it with the Andaman black stickers.

in-lm-548836.title: Pole: metal with one very long top bar
in-lm-548836.summary: Metal pole with a generic crossbar plus a very long bar extending to one side at the top that holds the insulators.

in-lm-548837.title: Sticker: yellow pole stickers also in the capital
in-lm-548837.summary: Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, the capital can rarely have yellow stickers too. These regions all look very different.

in-lm-548838.title: Pole: mesh pole with pyramid extension
in-lm-548838.summary: A mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides attached to a pyramid-shaped extension. It must be a pole, not a much bigger phone tower. Around Hyderabad.

in-lm-548839.title: Pole: metal poles with telephone-speaker tops
in-lm-548839.summary: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram, metal poles whose tops look like telephone speakers are common, in several variants.

in-lm-548841.title: Pole: 1.5 trapezoids
in-lm-548841.summary: This pole configuration is mainly in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-548845.title: Pole: extra bar underneath plus small top crossbar
in-lm-548845.summary: Poles in Tripura often have an extra bar underneath as well as the small crossbar on top.

in-lm-548846.title: Pole: trident with asymmetric crossbar
in-lm-548846.summary: A pole with an asymmetric crossbar, one side double the length, with two insulators on the long side and one on the short side. About 95% Telangana, but rare. The bar itself must be asymmetric.

in-lm-548847.title: Pole: T-shaped extension with three insulators
in-lm-548847.summary: A T-shaped pole extension with 3 insulators: 45% Andhra Pradesh, 45% Telangana, 9% Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-548848.title: Pole: triangle-shaped window insulators on crossbar
in-lm-548848.summary: Triangle-shaped window insulators on a crossbar: 90% Jharkhand, 2% Chhattisgarh, 1% Bihar.

in-lm-548849.title: Pole: only a tiny crossbar on top
in-lm-548849.summary: A pole with no top except a tiny bar is often in Odisha (70-80%).

in-lm-548850.title: Pole: small ring-like bar attached at both ends
in-lm-548850.summary: Like a second vertical bar, but attached at both ends, giving a ring shape, and close to the pole. About 35% Maharashtra, 35% Madhya Pradesh, 20% Chhattisgarh.

in-lm-548851.title: Pole: big rectangular metal ring around the pole
in-lm-548851.summary: A big rectangular metal ring around the pole. Most common in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Tripura.

in-lm-548852.title: Pole: metal crossbar with no insulators
in-lm-548852.summary: A metal crossbar with no insulators. Most common in Maharashtra (50%), also occasionally in other northern states. In the north-east it is exclusive to Tripura.

in-lm-548853.title: Pole: pure metal pole in the north-west Himalaya
in-lm-548853.summary: Pure metal poles are usually more common in the north-east Himalaya. If you see them in the north-west, it is most likely Uttarakhand.

in-lm-548854.title: Pole: 3-5 insulators pointing up
in-lm-548854.summary: Three to five insulators pointing up, attached to the pole. Common in Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Bihar.

in-lm-548855.title: Pole: insulators on top in one direction, bare bar below
in-lm-548855.summary: Insulators at the top, attached directly to the concrete and pointing one way, with a bare metal crossbar below. About 70% Maharashtra, 10% Chhattisgarh, 5% Himachal Pradesh.

in-lm-548856.title: Pole: small trapezoid, diagonals short of crossbar end
in-lm-548856.summary: A trapezoid pole top where the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar. Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh, sometimes Tripura.

in-lm-548857.title: Pole: hollow metal pole, C-shaped from above
in-lm-548857.summary: An indent runs through the whole pole, so from above it looks like a C. Most common in Mizoram, also in Himachal Pradesh and sometimes central states.

in-lm-548858.title: Pole: silver pole with red or brown top
in-lm-548858.summary: Silver-painted poles with a red or brown top. Common in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Tripura and Mizoram.

in-lm-548859.title: Pole: metal poles with red or yellow stripes
in-lm-548859.summary: Metal poles in Uttarakhand sometimes have red or yellow stripes painted on them.

in-lm-548860.title: Sign: white metal plate, sometimes rusty
in-lm-548860.summary: A white metal plate that can be rusted and browner. Found in northern states: Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, sometimes Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

in-lm-548861.title: Landscape: forests and dark brown soil
in-lm-548861.summary: West of the Western Ghats in Maharashtra: lots of forest and dark brown soil. It looks a bit like Kerala but with fewer palms.

in-lm-548862.title: Pole: overly complicated dark metal pole
in-lm-548862.summary: An overly complicated pole, usually dark metal. 90% West Bengal.

in-lm-548863.title: Pole: skinny pole with one or two small bars near the top
in-lm-548863.summary: A metal or concrete pole, skinnier than a generic pole, with one or two small bars near the top. Not exclusive to Maharashtra but very common there.

in-lm-548864.title: Landscape: dark soil with trident poles
in-lm-548864.summary: Dark soil is usually in and around Maharashtra. With trident poles it puts you in northern Karnataka, usually near the Maharashtra border.

in-lm-548865.title: Pole: vertical bar on top, attached with two short bars
in-lm-548865.summary: A vertical bar at the pole top attached with two short bars not at its ends (that would be a ring pole). About 50% Chhattisgarh, 30% Madhya Pradesh, 15% Maharashtra, 10% West Bengal.

in-lm-548866.title: Pole: triangle pole top
in-lm-548866.summary: About 32% each Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, 1% each Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

in-lm-548867.title: Pole: extended vertical bar sticking far above the pole
in-lm-548867.summary: An extra vertical bar at the pole top that extends well above the pole. 85% West Bengal, 12% Chhattisgarh.

in-lm-548868.title: Pole: short extra bar on top
in-lm-548868.summary: A short bar at the top of the pole. Mostly Rajasthan and Telangana, sometimes Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra. In the north-east, Tripura or rarely Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-548869.title: Pole: generic top with grey crossbar
in-lm-548869.summary: A generic pole top with a grey crossbar is most likely Uttar Pradesh, less often Odisha or Bihar. In South India it is 98% Kerala.

in-lm-548870.title: Pole: symmetric trident
in-lm-548870.summary: About 60% Tamil Nadu, 20% Telangana, 15% Andhra Pradesh. The crossbar must be symmetric; asymmetric is usually Telangana.

in-lm-548871.title: Landscape: wetter, greener western plains
in-lm-548871.summary: The western plains (Punjab, Haryana, west Uttar Pradesh) look wetter and greener than the general Ganges valley, often with rice and sugarcane. Not 100% reliable.

in-lm-548872.title: Coverage: double smudge on camera
in-lm-548872.summary: A double smudge is found in the central-north of a wildlife sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh.

in-lm-576248.title: Ads: Ultra Tech cement, anywhere but north-east
in-lm-576248.summary: Ultra Tech cement signs are found anywhere except north-east India.

in-lm-576462.title: Ads: Max cement, north-east only
in-lm-576462.summary: Max cement is found only in the north-east, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-576463.title: Ads: Duraguard cement
in-lm-576463.summary: Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, sometimes Odisha. Don't confuse with Duraton.

in-lm-576464.title: Ads: Double Bull cement
in-lm-576464.summary: Found in central and east India, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes Gujarat.

in-lm-576465.title: Ads: Chettinad cement with C logo
in-lm-576465.summary: Recognisable by a C logo. Found in South India, and sometimes Goa and Maharashtra.

in-lm-576466.title: Ads: Ramco cement
in-lm-576466.summary: Found in South India, less common in Karnataka. Sometimes in West Bengal.

in-lm-576467.title: Ads: Zuari cement
in-lm-576467.summary: Found in South India, especially Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-576468.title: Ads: Bangur cement
in-lm-576468.summary: Found in large parts of India. Only sometimes in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi. Never in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, the north-east, Gujarat or north of Himachal Pradesh.

in-lm-576469.title: Ads: JK Lakshmi cement
in-lm-576469.summary: Found in north and central India plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat, sometimes Maharashtra. Don't confuse with JK Power Cement.

in-lm-576470.title: Ads: Shree cement
in-lm-576470.summary: Found everywhere except Himalayan states, the north-east, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-576472.title: Ads: Sanghi cement with lion logo
in-lm-576472.summary: Recognisable by a lion logo. Found only in Gujarat.

in-lm-576473.title: Ads: HiBond cement with wavy triangle logo
in-lm-576473.summary: Recognisable by a wavy triangle logo. Found only in Gujarat.

in-lm-576474.title: Ads: Ambuja cement
in-lm-576474.summary: Common everywhere except the north-east, where it sometimes appears in Assam.

in-lm-576476.title: Roads: tile-paved roads, even rural ones
in-lm-576476.summary: Many roads in Assam are paved with tiles, and this stands out because it also appears on very rural roads.

in-lm-576477.title: Crops: tea in the east and south of the state
in-lm-576477.summary: In Assam, tea is mostly in the east and south, with some patches in the west.

in-lm-576478.title: Crops: tea near the northern border
in-lm-576478.summary: In West Bengal, tea plantations are near the northern border with Bhutan.

differs.how: Tea near the northern Bhutan border

in-lm-576479.title: Vehicles: vans with yellow plates in the north-east
in-lm-576479.summary: Vans, white, red or orange, with yellow plates in north-east India are only in West Bengal and Assam. A white plate does not count.

in-lm-576480.title: Houses: red brick, concentrated in the northern plains
in-lm-576480.summary: Red brick is everywhere, but notably concentrated in the Ganges valley, especially towards the west.

in-lm-576481.title: Roadside: concrete blocks, like in Bhutan
in-lm-576481.summary: Concrete blocks like those in Bhutan are common in, but not limited to, north-east India.

in-lm-576482.title: Plants: eucalyptus in the northern foothills
in-lm-576482.summary: Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby Uttar Pradesh.

in-lm-576483.title: Clothing: boat-shaped white cap
in-lm-576483.summary: The Gandhi cap, a boat-shaped white hat, is almost unique to Maharashtra. White hats are also common among Muslims, so check it is boat-shaped.

in-lm-576485.title: Ads: IELTS exam adverts
in-lm-576485.summary: IELTS exam ads are fairly common between Punjab and western Uttar Pradesh, though they can appear anywhere.

in-lm-576486.title: Plants: jand tree with leaf clusters on thick branches
in-lm-576486.summary: The jand tree has clusters of leaves at the ends of thick branches. Found in northern Rajasthan and southern Haryana and Punjab.

in-lm-576487.title: Ads: Wonder cement
in-lm-576487.summary: Found north-west of Madhya Pradesh, but not in Himachal Pradesh or further north.

in-lm-576489.title: Plate: first two letters show the state
in-lm-576489.summary: Unblurred plates, often on trucks, start with two letters giving the state, then two digits for the district. AP means Andhra Pradesh. Plates not starting with letters, or starting with T0, are national.

in-lm-576491.title: Google car: boxy car with an extra step at the front
in-lm-576491.summary: A boxy car with an extra step at the front is found in Odisha.

in-lm-576492.title: Ads: Star cement
in-lm-576492.summary: Found in north-east India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.

in-lm-576493.title: Houses: very strong colors like pink and purple
in-lm-576493.summary: Houses with very strong colours like dark yellow, pink and purple are often in Tamil Nadu, sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.

in-lm-576494.title: Coverage: oddly dark footage in daytime
in-lm-576494.summary: Many locations in Tripura look quite dark even though the sun is out and not setting.

in-lm-576495.title: Landscape: wonky undulating hills
in-lm-576495.summary: The hills in Odisha are very wonky: undulating and varying greatly in height.

in-lm-576496.title: Plants: blue pine, drooping needles in all directions
in-lm-576496.summary: Blue pine has well-visible branches with thin brush of new needles at the edges, needles drooping in all directions, and a conical crown at height. Mostly far west Arunachal Pradesh and the road south of Harsil.

in-lm-576503.title: Ads: Mycem cement
in-lm-576503.summary: Found only in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

in-lm-576504.title: Ads: Duraton cement
in-lm-576504.summary: Only in Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir. Don't confuse with Duraguard.

in-lm-576505.title: Ads: Concreto cement
in-lm-576505.summary: Found in east India: Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha.

in-lm-576506.title: Ads: Konark cement
in-lm-576506.summary: Found in Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

in-lm-576507.title: Ads: Bangur Power cement
in-lm-576507.summary: Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, sometimes Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh. Different distribution from Bangur Cement.

in-lm-576508.title: Ads: JSW cement
in-lm-576508.summary: Found in South India, Goa, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

in-lm-576510.title: Plants: Himalayan hemlock, two rows of short needles
in-lm-576510.summary: A twig with two symmetrical rows of short needles, downward-bending twigs and slightly untidy crowns. Found south of Senge and Dirang in west Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-576511.title: Plants: larch with no needles in winter
in-lm-576511.summary: A conical, Christmas-tree shape with lighter needles if present, bare in winter (all coverage). Around Senge and sometimes Manda La in Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-576512.title: Plants: spruce with clumped needles, extremely rare
in-lm-576512.summary: Needles in separate clumps, darker than pines, with new shoots and buds visible from afar. Only one tree found, at Manda La.

in-lm-576513.title: Plants: Morinda spruce, dense foliage, draping shoots
in-lm-576513.summary: Dense foliage with shoots draping downward. Found in Himachal Pradesh (Shimla, Kullu, Manali) and Uttarakhand (Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Ukhimath).

in-lm-576514.title: Pole: black and white stripes low on the pole
in-lm-576514.summary: White and black stripes at the bottom of a pole are in Meghalaya and Tripura. Don't confuse with the Tamil Nadu white-black-white paint, which is higher up.

in-lm-576515.title: Vehicles: black auto rickshaws with yellow roofs
in-lm-576515.summary: Auto rickshaws with a black body and yellow roof, the reverse of the Andhra/Telangana style, are common in Nagaland.

in-lm-576516.title: Houses: short curtain hanging down the side of roofs
in-lm-576516.summary: Roofs in Sikkim often have a short curtain hanging down at the side.

in-lm-576517.title: Walls: dark rock walls around one city
in-lm-576517.summary: Dark rock walls are common around Udaipur in Rajasthan.

in-lm-576518.title: Pole: orange pole paint on one highway
in-lm-576518.summary: This orange pole paint is on NH15 in Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-576519.title: Crops: tea along two borders
in-lm-576519.summary: In Tripura, tea is along the Bangladesh border and the Assam border.

in-lm-576520.title: Landscape: dark volcanic rock with white mineral patches
in-lm-576520.summary: A volcanic rock, dark with white mineral patches, mostly between Pune and Jalgaon. The dark rock without patches is more widespread.

in-lm-576521.title: Road: divided concrete road with dark metal poles
in-lm-576521.summary: The NH51 in Gujarat is lined with dark metal poles, unlike most of Gujarat's concrete holey poles. It is also divided and paved with concrete.

in-lm-576522.title: Clothing: lungi, towel-like wrap at the waist
in-lm-576522.summary: People wearing a lungi, which looks like a towel wrapped around the waist, are more common in South India.

in-lm-576523.title: Statues: horseman statue with orange flag
in-lm-576523.summary: Statues of Shivaji, always on a horse and often with an orange flag, are common in Maharashtra.

in-lm-576524.title: Landscape: reddish or pinkish soil towards the east
in-lm-576524.summary: In Madhya Pradesh, reddish or pinkish soil is more common towards the east.

in-lm-576525.title: Clothing: colorful scarves
in-lm-576525.summary: People wearing colourful scarves are generally in the north of India.

in-lm-576526.title: Landscape: elevated roads in dry land, like Bangladesh
in-lm-576526.summary: Elevated roads with a dry landscape, similar to Bangladesh, are common in and around Jharkhand.

in-lm-576527.title: Bollard: white-black-white, like Thailand's
in-lm-576527.summary: Thai-style bollards, white-black-white, are found in Odisha.

in-lm-576528.title: Pole: thin rusted hollow pole
in-lm-576528.summary: Thin, rusted poles that are hollow, with an indent from bottom to top, are found in Maharashtra and sometimes Chhattisgarh.

in-lm-583882.title: Plants: fir with symmetrical shoots, small triangle shoots
in-lm-583882.summary: Symmetrical shoots, longer needles, small shoots forming triangles, and separated clusters at different heights. Found at Senge and Manda La in Arunachal Pradesh.

in-lm-583883.title: Plants: narrow conical fir with layered clusters
in-lm-583883.summary: Symmetrical branches in layered clusters, narrow conical shape and dense foliage. Found around Jibhi, Chinyalisour and Ukhimath, sometimes Shimla and the Dehradun-Rishikesh range.

in-lm-598743.title: Houses: very high red roofs, traditional courtyard houses
in-lm-598743.summary: Traditional courtyard houses (nalukettu) have distinct, often very high, red roofs. Often found around the south-west backwaters.

in-lm-598744.title: Plants: cypress with draping thin twigs
in-lm-598744.summary: Thin twigs with symmetrical needles draping down, most visible from below the crown. Mostly west Sikkim and several spots in Arunachal Pradesh, rarely West Bengal near the Sikkim border.

in-lm-603203.title: Flag: unofficial state flag, horizontal stripes
in-lm-603203.summary: This is the unofficial flag of Karnataka, with horizontal stripes.

in-lm-603290.title: Symbols: Jain symbols
in-lm-603290.summary: Jainism is a rare minority religion. Jain symbols are mostly in Maharashtra, then Gujarat and Rajasthan, then Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.

in-lm-603291.title: Flag: Sarnaism flag and symbol
in-lm-603291.summary: These stand for Sarnaism, very localised around Ranchi and southern Jharkhand.

in-lm-603292.title: Flag: red disc on white, Donyi Polo
in-lm-603292.summary: A flag resembling the Japanese flag stands for Donyi Polo, a religion in Arunachal Pradesh between Ziro and Anini.

in-lm-603295.title: Flag: blue flag with symbol, Navayana Buddhism
in-lm-603295.summary: A blue flag with a symbol in the middle is specific to Navayana Buddhism, common in central-eastern Maharashtra.

in-lm-605405.title: Flag: Trinamool party flag, flowers on grass
in-lm-605405.summary: The party flag often shows flowers on grass over the Indian flag. Mainly in West Bengal, less in the north of it, sometimes west Meghalaya.

in-lm-605406.title: Flag: orange-red-green with table lamp
in-lm-605406.summary: This party has an orange-red-green flag with a table lamp symbol and operates only in Sikkim.

in-lm-605407.title: Flag: green-white-yellow separatist flag
in-lm-605407.summary: A green-white-yellow flag found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.

in-lm-605408.title: Flag: yellow-grey-dark red with landscape and Devanagari
in-lm-605408.summary: A yellow, grey and dark red flag with a landscape in the middle and Devanagari text at the top. Found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.

in-lm-605409.title: Flag: Bodoland party flag
in-lm-605409.summary: This flag, with a tool on an Indian background, is found in Bodoland, the Assam districts bordering Bhutan.

in-lm-605410.title: Flag: yellow-white-green with farmer on tractor
in-lm-605410.summary: A yellow, white and green flag with a farmer on a tractor, found in Bodoland. Not the green-white-yellow separatist flag.

in-lm-605411.title: Flag: elephant on a tricolor
in-lm-605411.summary: The party flag shows an elephant on a horizontal tricolor like the Dutch flag. It operates only in Assam.

in-lm-605412.title: Flag: black and red flag
in-lm-605412.summary: A black and red flag. Other black-and-red objects are also common in Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-605413.title: Flag: blue and red with star
in-lm-605413.summary: A blue and red flag with a star, found only in Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-611952.title: Flag: tiger symbol of a regional party
in-lm-611952.summary: The flag of a party active only in Tamil Nadu. The tiger symbol sometimes appears without the flag.

in-lm-612029.title: Colors: dark red, black and white tribal colors
in-lm-612029.summary: The Karbi people live in two districts of Assam. Their flag is rare, but you often see their colours, dark red, black and white, there.

in-lm-612193.title: Flag: regional party flag
in-lm-612193.summary: The flag of a party active only in Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-612258.title: Flag: Meitei flag around the valley city
in-lm-612258.summary: The Meitei people live in Manipur, especially Imphal. Their flag is common in and around that city.

in-lm-612330.title: Flag: ceiling fan symbol
in-lm-612330.summary: This party is exclusive to Andhra Pradesh and most popular in the south. Its symbol is a ceiling fan.

in-lm-612331.title: Flag: bicycle symbol
in-lm-612331.summary: This party is exclusive to Uttar Pradesh and its symbol is a bicycle.

in-lm-612332.title: Google car: most common island car
in-lm-612332.summary: This is the most common, though not the only, car in the Andaman islands.

in-lm-612333.title: Flag: green with half moon and star
in-lm-612333.summary: A green flag with a half moon and star pointing to the top left. This party is almost exclusively in Kerala, mostly in Kozhikode and Malappuram.

in-lm-612334.title: Vehicles: only e-rickshaws, often blue
in-lm-612334.summary: West Bengal has only e-rickshaws, with a unique shape, often blue.

in-lm-612335.title: Flag: green-white-green with arrow
in-lm-612335.summary: The flag is green-white-green with an arrow symbol. Found only in Bihar.

in-lm-621152.title: Flag: yellow and red vertical stripes
in-lm-621152.summary: This is the flag of a party specific to Tripura, with two vertical stripes, yellow and red. Don't confuse with the Karnataka flag, whose stripes are horizontal.

in-lm-621431.title: Flag: lotus flower, flags everywhere
in-lm-621431.summary: The BJP is a popular national party, so its flags are everywhere. Its symbol is a lotus. Most popular in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.

in-lm-621432.title: Flag: open hand on the tricolor
in-lm-621432.summary: INC is a popular national party found almost everywhere, except West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, where regional versions exist. Its symbol is a flat hand on the Indian tricolor.

in-lm-82169.title: Wind farms: where they cluster
in-lm-82169.summary: Wind farms are most common in four states (Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu). Rough areas: south-west half of Gujarat; central Karnataka; far south and around Coimbatore; Maharashtra near the Madhya and Gujarat borders; Rajasthan between Jodhpur and Jaisalmer; west and north of Indore.

in-lm-82266.title: Landscape: snowy high mountain road
in-lm-82266.summary: On the NH3 in northern Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border, snow is visible from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai.

in-lm-82267.title: Pole: triangle top with three insulators on top
in-lm-82267.summary: Triangle pole tops with three insulators on top are found in the far north (Jammu and Kashmir), sometimes Himachal Pradesh. Not to be confused with ordinary triangle tops found elsewhere, and not 100% unique.

in-lm-823.title: Pole: white-black-white stripe on poles and trees
in-lm-823.summary: Poles and trees in the far south have a white-black-white marking.

in-lm-824.title: Electricity meter: mint to grey-green design
in-lm-824.summary: Mint green to greyish-green meters of this design appear in the north-west (Punjab, Haryana).

in-lm-825.title: Pole paint: four yellow-black stripes
in-lm-825.summary: Four yellow and black stripes on poles usually place you in the north-east plains (Bihar). It occasionally appears in the capital region, where 5 or more is more common. 3 or 5 stripes are rare in Bihar.

in-lm-826.title: Pole paint: five or more yellow-black stripes
in-lm-826.summary: Five or more black and yellow stripes on poles are usually only in the capital region. Rare elsewhere, like Bihar. Sometimes fewer than 5 appear in the capital.

in-lm-89689.title: Plants: coconut palms near coasts and in the south
in-lm-89689.summary: Coconut palms are most common in the south-west, the west of Karnataka and the south-west coast. In general they grow near coasts, near the Bangladesh border, and anywhere south of central Telangana.

in-lm-89690.title: Landscape: tall brick-kiln chimneys
in-lm-89690.summary: In poorer parts of the northern plains, villages build large chimneys to fire bricks. Visible from afar, they are a good clue for Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, and also fairly common in poorer east Tamil Nadu.

in-lm-89692.title: Houses: W-shaped roof tiles on the west coast
in-lm-89692.summary: W-shaped tiles are mostly on the west coast and in the far south, but reach inland into western Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

in-lm-89694.title: Houses: plain flat roof tiles
in-lm-89694.summary: Flat tiles are the plainest type. Mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar Pradesh.

in-lm-89695.title: Houses: U-shaped tiles with flat connecting tiles
in-lm-89695.summary: Tiles with a U shape and a flatter tile linking them. Very common in south-east Uttar Pradesh and west Bihar, rare in north-east Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

in-lm-89696.title: Houses: roofs of staple-shaped flat tiles
in-lm-89696.summary: A roof full of staple-shaped tiles, found around Prayagraj in the south-east of Uttar Pradesh.

in-lm-89697.title: Landscape: dry north-south mountain ranges, wind turbines
in-lm-89697.summary: A valley with wind turbines along the ridges. It may be the only place in India with big dry north-south ranges both west and east of you, so click here with a good north-south angle. Differs from the Maharashtra west coast mountains, which have different angles.

in-luxm.title: Pole: mix of even and uneven top
in-luxm.summary: In the north-east you may find poles combining an even and an uneven top.

in-m0b1.title: Pole: trident with middle tip bent 90 degrees
in-m0b1.summary: Trident pole tops with the middle tip bent at a right angle are found in the north-east (Assam).

in-m582.title: Houses: wealthy modern homes in two developed states
in-m582.summary: Two of the most developed states (Goa, Kerala) often have very wealthy, modern homes.

in-mlRC.title: Plants: doum palms with several branches
in-mlRC.summary: Doum palms look like palmyra palms but with several branches. They are almost only on one small western union territory (Diu).

in-nEx6.title: Vehicles: yellow tuk tuks with black roofs
in-nEx6.summary: Yellow auto rickshaws with black roofs are common in the south and south-east states (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu). They rarely appear elsewhere.

in-offm.title: Crops: cotton in the west
in-offm.summary: Cotton is common in western India, especially Gujarat and Maharashtra.

in-ohMv.title: Pole: square concrete with trident top
in-ohMv.summary: The most common pole is square concrete with a trident top. Many regions have their own pole types. Poles are almost always concrete or metal; wood is extremely rare.

in-ov4H.title: Pole paint: five or more thin black-yellow stripes
in-ov4H.summary: Pole paint of five or more thin black and yellow stripes is found in the capital region (Delhi).

in-pFp5.title: Plants: pines with hanging downward needles
in-pFp5.summary: The Bhutan white pine has hanging, downward-pointing needles. It is mainly in a far north-east valley and near the Bhutan border in Arunachal Pradesh.

in-pdE8.title: Language: English as an official language
in-pdE8.summary: English is an official language and appears on many signs.

in-q0Vn.title: Google car: thin grey antenna, good quality
in-q0Vn.summary: Coverage on NH326 west of Brahmapur has a thin grey antenna and unusually high quality for this camera, especially near a reservoir.

in-qGEO.title: Pole: black sticker with digits and middle arrow
in-qGEO.summary: On the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, black pole stickers with several digits and an arrow in the middle.

in-rS5H.title: Plate: long; white, yellow commercial, green EV
in-rS5H.summary: Plates are fairly long. Most are white, commercial vehicles use yellow, and electric vehicles use green.

in-rfjr.title: Landscape: distinctly dark soil
in-rfjr.summary: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in the west (Maharashtra) and adjacent regions.

in-sTsG.title: Landscape: V-shaped green valleys, smooth ridge tops
in-sTsG.summary: South of Shillong, green eroded V-shaped valleys with fairly flat, smooth ridge tops. Mizoram hills are less smooth, with more ups and downs.

in-sV6b.title: Houses: flat tiles with small diamond bump
in-sV6b.summary: Flat roof tiles like those in the south, but with a small diamond-shaped bump in the middle, are common in and around the east (West Bengal).

in-sf3g.title: Vehicles: black taxis with yellow roofs
in-sf3g.summary: Black taxis with yellow roofs appear in one north-east state and in the big west-coast city.

in-sjLQ.title: Pole: poles split in two sections, like Brazil's
in-sjLQ.summary: Poles divided in two sections, like Brazilian ones, are common in the south-east (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana).

differs.how: Brazilian poles look alike but have other differences

in-t17C.title: Infrastructure: elevated railways in eight cities
in-t17C.summary: Elevated railways exist in Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kochi, Kolkata and Mumbai.

in-tANX.title: Houses: metal roofs with small triangle near the top
in-tANX.summary: Metal roofs with a small triangle near the top are common in the north-east.

in-txPI.title: Landscape: flat fertile northern plains
in-txPI.summary: The northern plains, the Ganges valley, are very fertile with extremely flat, open fields.

in-uMaZ.title: Houses: square panels separated by thin beams
in-uMaZ.summary: Houses made of square panels divided by thin beams are found in the north-east.

in-uZ19.title: Pole paint: exactly four thick black-yellow stripes
in-uZ19.summary: Pole paint of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes is found in the north-east plains (Bihar).

in-vWlV.title: Landscape: salt flats and coastal marsh, almost no plants
in-vWlV.summary: In parts of Gujarat, salt flats and coastal marshes with almost no plants but short yellow or brown grass, and shallow water. West Rajasthan has sandier soil and desert shrubs.

in-vs2g.title: Sign: black-and-white striped signposts
in-vs2g.summary: Signposts are often striped black and white. Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka have them too.

in-xTJB.title: Landscape: red soil in several regions
in-xTJB.summary: Red soil is found near the southern west coast and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

in-xtEg.title: Electricity meter: mint green with small window squares
in-xtEg.summary: In the north-west (Punjab), electricity meters are usually mint green with small window-like squares. Rarely seen in Haryana.

in-z2vE.title: Plants: Himalayan cedar on mountain roads
in-z2vE.summary: Himalayan cedar is most common on NH34 from Harsil to Gangotri and around Shimla.

in-zBTL.title: Pole: two diagonal bars forming a < shape
in-zBTL.summary: Poles with two diagonal bars in a < shape are common in two north-east states (Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh) and occasionally Assam.

in-zGL3.title: Pole: upside-down A bar below pole top
in-zGL3.summary: In the centre (Madhya Pradesh), poles often have an upside-down A-shaped metal bar slightly below the top.
